title: Illinois's 8th Congressional District election, 2026
description: Illinois's 8th Congressional District is an open seat in the 2026 general election after incumbent Democrat Raja Krishnamoorthi vacated the seat to run for the U.S. Senate. The district covers parts of Cook, DuPage, Kane, and McHenry counties, including communities such as Schaumburg, Elgin, and parts of Chicago's Far Northwest Side. The race pits former three-term Democratic Congresswoman Melissa Bean against Republican tech entrepreneur Jennifer Davis. The district has been redrawn to be solidly Democratic, and Bean won a competitive eight-way primary with significant support from pro-Israel super PACs.
polling_note: No general election matchup polls between Melissa Bean and Jennifer Davis were available as of mid-2026. The Cook Political Report rates the race as Solid D / Solidly Democratic.

candidates.name: Melissa Bean
candidates.summary: Melissa Bean is a former U.S. Representative who served Illinois's 8th Congressional District from 2005 to 2011. She won the 2026 Democratic primary with 32% of the vote in an eight-candidate field, positioning herself to reclaim the seat she lost to Joe Walsh in the 2010 Tea Party wave. Bean has campaigned on a moderate platform emphasizing pragmatism over polarization, criticizing the Trump administration, and has been buoyed by over $7 million in outside spending, including from pro-Israel groups.

candidates.name: Jennifer Davis
candidates.summary: Jennifer Davis is a tech entrepreneur and political outsider who won the 2026 Republican primary for Illinois's 8th Congressional District with 51% of the vote. She co-founded Davisware with her husband at age 17 and grew it into a global service technology company before selling to Serent Capital. Davis, a mother of ten, has positioned herself as a pragmatic conservative focused on cutting red tape, supporting small businesses, and putting families first, and has been endorsed by several local Republican leaders.
